page_title: Inside Atlassian: how IT & SRE use ChatOps to run incident management

sources.entry: Inside Atlassian: how IT & SRE use ChatOps to run incident management

summary.name: Atlassian ChatOps incident management process
summary.one_liner: A 2016 Atlassian blog post describing how its SRE teams run production incident management through HipChat-based ChatOps integrated with Jira Service Desk, Datadog, PagerDuty and Statuspage.
use_cases: Running incident response in a team chat room
Creating a dedicated chat room per incident
Routing monitoring alerts into team chat
Writing post-incident reviews from chat logs
Tracking incident tickets alongside chat discussion
summary.what_it_does: The article explains how Atlassian's SRE teams use chat as the hub for reliability work. Monitoring and ticketing tools such as Datadog, PagerDuty, Jira Service Desk and Statuspage post alerts into team chat rooms, where teams verify and assess severity. A Jira Service Desk ticket on a critical component automatically creates a dedicated "hot room" named after the issue key, and responders can view and update the issue from the chat sidebar. The chat log then serves as a transcript for post-incident review, and a Confluence page documents each incident. The page reports a 5x improvement in response speed internally, though it gives no detailed methodology.
notable: Automatic creation of incident-specific HipChat rooms from Jira Service Desk tickets
Ability to move Jira issues between states and add comments from within HipChat
Post-incident Confluence page created after each resolved incident
caveats: Describes Atlassian's own internal setup with HipChat, Jira Service Desk and related tools; not a standalone product
The 5x response speed figure is an internal measurement with no published method
Article is from 2016 and the tools described may have changed since
